mainTopic: Sources for the laws of slaughtering, offering up, sprinkling and other עבודות done outside the מקדש
overview: This amud asks where several laws about doing the עבודה outside the מקדש come from. First, רבא learns the אזהרה against שחיטת חוץ from רבי יונה's comparison of the two words שם in one פסוק. Next, the גמרא asks how we know a person is חייב for offering up outside a קרבן that was already slaughtered outside. רב כהנא, the school of רבי ישמעאל, and רבי יוחנן each give a source. רב ביבי objects that this would make the 36 כריתות in the משנה into 37, and the גמרא admits it is a קשיא. Then a ברייתא brings a מחלוקת between רבי ישמעאל and רבי עקיבא over which פסוק teaches the חיוב for sprinkling blood outside. The גמרא follows how each תנא uses the other's words: או זבח, יביאנו, לעשות אתו, דם יחשב, או אשר ישחט and זה הדבר. Along the way it brings rules about incomplete offerings, slaughtering a bird outside, and pinching a bird outside. Finally, the גמרא explains why one who takes a handful or collects blood outside is פטור: neither שחיטה nor זריקה can serve as a model to make him חייב.

steps.title: רבא learns the warning against slaughtering outside from Rabbi Yona's teaching
steps.stepSummary: רבא says the אזהרה for שחיטת חוץ comes from רבי יונה's teaching. The two words שם in one פסוק link slaughtering to offering up. Just as the Torah warned before it punished for offering up, it also warned before it punished for slaughtering.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: We learn it the way רבי יונה does. רבי יונה said: We learn it from the word 'there' and the word 'there.' Just as over there (offering up outside), the Torah did not give a punishment unless it also gave a warning, so too here (slaughtering outside), the Torah did not give a punishment unless it also gave a warning.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives one more answer to the earlier question: where does the Torah warn (אזהרה) against slaughtering a קרבן outside the בית המקדש?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק in דברים 12:14 says 'there' twice: once about offering up and once about 'doing' the קרבן, which includes slaughtering it. This joins the two acts together. The Torah never punishes with כרת without first giving a warning. So the punishment for slaughtering outside shows that a warning exists, even though no separate warning is spelled out.

keyTerms.meaning: It is learned from / it comes from (a comparison of words)
'There.' The word that appears twice in the פסוק and links the two acts
Gave a punishment
Gave a warning (אזהרה), meaning a clear prohibition
A Torah prohibition that must come before a punishment

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up 'punishment' and 'warning.' Everyone agrees there is a punishment (כרת) for slaughtering outside. The question is only where the warning is. A warning is needed before the Torah can punish.

phrases.english: Rava said: in accordance with Rabbi Yona,
as Rabbi Yona said:
It is learned from "there" and "there";
phrases.notes: Both words 'there' are in one פסוק: דברים 12:14.

phrases.english: just as over there, it did not punish
phrases.notes: 'Over there' is offering up outside. 'Here,' in the next lines, is slaughtering outside.

phrases.english: unless it also gave a warning,
so too here, it did not punish
unless it also gave a warning.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives another answer, alongside earlier answers on the דף, to the question of where the warning against שחיטת חוץ comes from.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The two words שם in דברים 12:14 link slaughtering to offering up. Since the Torah only punishes after a warning, the warning that exists for offering up also covers slaughtering.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The אזהרה for שחיטת חוץ is learned through the comparison of שם and שם, following רבי יונה.

steps.title: What about offering up outside an animal that was already slaughtered outside?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks a new question. The פסוק makes someone חייב for offering up outside a קרבן that was fit for the inside altar. What is the source that he is also חייב when the קרבן was slaughtered outside and could never go on the altar?
steps.simpleTranslation: We have found a source for offerings fit to be burned inside that someone offered up outside. Offerings that belong outside (because they were already slaughtered outside) that someone offered up outside: from where do we know he is חייב?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question and sets up the next steps. It looks for a source that a person is חייב for offering up outside even a קרבן that was already slaughtered outside.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק about offering up outside says 'and he did not bring it to the entrance of the אהל מועד.' That suggests it only covers a קרבן that could have been brought inside. A קרבן slaughtered outside can never be brought in. So we need a separate source to make him חייב for offering it up outside too.

keyTerms.meaning: We have found (a source for one case)
Offerings fit to be burned on the altar inside
Offerings that can no longer go inside, because they were slaughtered outside
He offered them up (burned them as a קרבן)
From where (do we learn this)?

phrases.english: We have found offerings fit to be burned inside
that he offered up outside;
offerings that belong outside, that he offered up outside,
phrases.notes: He means a קרבן already slaughtered outside, which can never go on the altar.

phrases.english: from where do we know?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the warning against slaughtering outside to a new question about being חייב for offering up outside.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source that one is חייב for offering up outside a קרבן that was already slaughtered outside.

steps.title: רב כהנא reads 'to them' as 'about the nearby section'
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא answers from the words ואלהם תאמר. He reads them as if they said 'about them,' meaning about the section right before, which deals with slaughtering outside.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב כהנא said: The verse says, 'And to them you shall say.' This means: about the nearby matters you shall say.
steps.whatsHappening: רב כהנא answers the question by reading the word ואלהם in a creative way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ואלהם, written with an א, sounds like ועליהם, written with an ע, which means 'about them.' So רב כהנא reads the פסוק as saying: tell them about the nearby section, the one about slaughtering outside. That makes the law of offering up outside apply even to animals slaughtered outside.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And to them you shall say' (ויקרא 17:8)
The nearby matters, meaning the section right before

phrases.english: Rav Kahana said: The verse says:
"And to them you shall say"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 17:8

phrases.english: about the nearby matters you shall say.
phrases.notes: He reads אלהם as if it were עליהם, 'about them,' meaning the section just before, about slaughtering outside.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question asked in step 2.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: ואלהם is read as 'about them': about the nearby section on slaughtering outside. So offering up outside is forbidden even for an animal slaughtered outside.

steps.title: רבא objects: the word means 'to them,' not 'about them'
steps.stepSummary: רבא challenges רב כהנא. The פסוק says ואליהם, 'to them,' not ועליהם, 'about them,' so his reading does not fit the words.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא objects to this: Is it written 'and about them'?! It is written 'and to them'!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא attacks רב כהנא's reading, saying the word in the פסוק does not mean what רב כהנא needs it to mean.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב כהנא's proof depends entirely on reading the word as 'about.' רבא points out that the actual word is spelled with an א and means 'to.' It simply tells משה to whom he should speak. So the word cannot be pointing to the nearby section.

keyTerms.meaning: He objects to it (a strong challenge)
Is it written...?! (it is not)
'And about them' (with an ע)

phrases.english: Rava objects to it:
Is it written "and about them"?!
"And to them" is written!
phrases.notes: 'To them' just means to אהרן, his sons and בני ישראל, the people משה is told to speak to.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reading of the פסוק in step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב כהנא's reading of ואלהם as 'about them.'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק is spelled with an א, meaning 'to them,' so it cannot refer to the nearby section.

steps.title: The school of רבי ישמעאל: the extra 'and' joins the two sections
steps.stepSummary: Instead, רבא learns it from the school of רבי ישמעאל. The 'and' at the start of ואלהם תאמר joins the section on slaughtering outside with the section on offering up outside. So one is חייב for offering up even an animal slaughtered outside.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is as the school of רבי ישמעאל taught: 'And to them you shall say' comes to mix the sections together.
steps.whatsHappening: After rejecting רב כהנא's reading, רבא gives a new source for the question in step 2, from the teaching of the school of רבי ישמעאל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This approach does not change what the word means. It looks at the letter ו, 'and,' which joins the new section to the one before it. Since the two sections are linked, offering up outside is forbidden even after the animal was already slaughtered outside.

keyTerms.meaning: A teaching from the school (בית מדרש) of רבי ישמעאל
To mix / to join together
Sections of the Torah

steps.whatToRemember: A person is חייב for offering up outside even a קרבן that was already slaughtered outside. The source is not רב כהנא's 'about them' reading. It is the 'and' in ואלהם, which joins the two sections, following the school of רבי ישמעאל.

phrases.english: Rather, as the school of Rabbi Yishmael taught:
"And to them you shall say"
comes to mix the sections together.
phrases.notes: The 'and' links the slaughtering-outside section with the offering-up-outside section.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces רב כהנא's rejected answer with a new source.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The 'and' in ואלהם תאמר joins the two sections, so one is חייב for offering up outside even an animal slaughtered outside.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The liability comes from joining the sections (לערב פרשיות), not from reading אלהם as עליהם.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן learns it from the repeated word 'bringing'
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן answers the question from step 2 another way. A גזירה שוה from the word 'bringing' teaches that offering up outside makes one חייב even for a קרבן that will be burned outside.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: We learn it from 'bringing' and 'bringing.' Just as there, it is about offerings that will be burned outside, so too here, it is about offerings that will be burned outside.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן gives a different source for the question from step 2: why is one חייב for offering up outside an animal that was slaughtered outside?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The section on slaughtering outside and the section on offering up outside both use the word 'bring.' In the slaughtering section, the animal was killed outside, so it is unfit and will end up burned outside. The shared word carries that same kind of animal over to the offering-up section, so one is חייב for offering it up too.

keyTerms.meaning: It comes (is learned) from. Introduces a source, often a גזירה שוה.
Bringing. The word 'bring' that appears in both sections.
Things burned outside. Unfit קרבנות that will never go on the inside altar.
Just as there ... so too here. The usual pattern of a comparison.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
It is learned from 'bringing' and 'bringing';
phrases.notes: Both sections use the word 'bring.' See ויקרא 17:4 and ויקרא 17:9.

phrases.english: just as there, it is about offerings that will be burned outside,
phrases.notes: 'There' means the section on slaughtering outside. That animal can no longer go on the altar.

phrases.english: so too here, it is about offerings that will be burned outside.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second source, next to the one from רבי ישמעאל's school in step 5, for the question from step 2.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A גזירה שוה from the word 'bringing' links offering up to slaughtering, so one is חייב for offering up an animal slaughtered outside.

steps.title: The count of 36 כריתות becomes 37
steps.stepSummary: רב ביבי challenges these sources. If offering up an animal slaughtered outside is its own separate case, the משנה's count of 36 כריתות would really be 37. The גמרא admits this is a difficulty.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ביבי challenged: What about the משנה that says there are 36 כריתות in the Torah? There would be 37, because there is one who offers up and another who offers up! The גמרא says: It is a difficulty.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ביבי attacks the sources just given by using the count in the משנה of כריתות. The גמרא leaves the question unanswered.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה lists offering up outside as only one כרת case. The sources above seem to make two separate cases: offering up an animal slaughtered inside, and offering up an animal slaughtered outside. That would make the total 37 instead of 36, and the גמרא has no answer.

keyTerms.meaning: He challenged it. Introduces a strong objection.
Cases where the punishment is כרת.
One who offers up on an altar.
It is a difficulty. The question stands with no answer.

steps.confusionAlert: The word קשיא at the end does not cancel the halacha. It only means the גמרא has no good answer to רב ביבי's counting problem.

phrases.english: Rav Beivai challenged it:
What about that which we learned in a משנה:
There are thirty-six cases of כרת in the Torah.
But there would be thirty-seven,
since there is one who offers up, and another one who offers up!
phrases.notes: One offers up an animal slaughtered inside, and the other offers up an animal slaughtered outside. That makes two separate cases.

phrases.english: It is a difficulty.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב בִּיבִי, הָא דִּתְנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the sources given in steps 3, 5, and 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: The sources that make one חייב for offering up an animal slaughtered outside.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If these are two separate prohibitions, the count of כריתות in the משנה would be 37, not 36.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the count of 36 כריתות is used as a check against reading the פסוקים as more separate prohibitions.

steps.title: Where do we learn the rule for sprinkling part of the blood outside?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens a new topic: the משנה says that one who sprinkles even part of the blood outside is חייב. What is the source?
steps.simpleTranslation: And about what we learned in a משנה, that one who sprinkles some of the blood outside is חייב: where do we learn this from?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new question about sprinkling blood outside. This sets up the next step, which gives the source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוקים clearly speak about slaughtering outside and offering up outside. Sprinkling blood is a different act, so the גמרא needs a source for it. The משנה also says that even part of the blood is enough.

keyTerms.meaning: One who sprinkles (the blood of a קרבן).
Part of the blood, for example one sprinkling instead of all of them.
From where do we know this? Asks for a source.

phrases.english: And about that which we learned in a משנה:
One who sprinkles part of the blood outside is liable,
from where do we derive this?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָדִתְנַן: הַזּוֹרֵק מִקְצָת דָּמִים בַּחוּץ – חַיָּיב, מְנָלַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the topic of offering up outside to a new topic, sprinkling blood outside.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source for being חייב for sprinkling blood outside.

steps.title: רבי ישמעאל learns it from 'דם יחשב,' and רבי עקיבא from 'או זבח'
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא gives two sources. רבי ישמעאל learns it from 'דם יחשב.' רבי עקיבא learns it from 'או זבח.'
steps.simpleTranslation: He learns it from a ברייתא: 'Blood shall be counted' comes to include one who sprinkles. These are the words of רבי ישמעאל. רבי עקיבא says: 'Or a sacrifice' comes to include one who sprinkles.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a ברייתא in which two תנאים each give a different פסוק as the source for sprinkling outside.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי ישמעאל reads the word 'blood' in the slaughtering section as adding the act of sprinkling blood. רבי עקיבא reads the extra word 'or' in the offering-up section as adding sprinkling. Both agree that one is חייב; they only argue about which פסוק teaches it.

keyTerms.meaning: He derives it (from).
From what was taught in a ברייתא.
To include. The extra word adds another case.
Blood shall be counted (against him).
Or a sacrifice.

steps.whatToRemember: Sprinkling blood outside makes one חייב. רבי ישמעאל learns it from 'דם יחשב' and רבי עקיבא learns it from 'או זבח.'

phrases.english: He derives it from that which is taught in a ברייתא:
'Blood shall be counted' comes to include one who sprinkles.
phrases.notes: ויקרא 17:4

phrases.english: These are the words of Rabbi Yishmael.
Rabbi Akiva says:
'Or a sacrifice' comes to include one who sprinkles.
phrases.notes: ויקרא 17:8

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question from step 8.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי ישמעאל: from 'דם יחשב.' רבי עקיבא: from 'או זבח.'

steps.title: What does רבי ישמעאל learn from 'או זבח'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what רבי ישמעאל does with the words 'או זבח,' since he does not use them for sprinkling.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי ישמעאל, what does he do with this 'or a sacrifice'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what רבי ישמעאל learns from רבי עקיבא's word, since every word in the Torah should teach something. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא used 'או זבח' for sprinkling. רבי ישמעאל used a different פסוק for that, so he must need 'או' for something else.

keyTerms.meaning: What does he do with it? What does he learn from this word?

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yishmael,
what does he do with this 'or a sacrifice'?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל, הַאי ״אוֹ זָבַח״ מַאי עָבֵיד לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows up on the מחלוקת in step 9.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How רבי ישמעאל uses the word 'או' in 'או זבח.'

steps.title: 'Or' teaches that each case counts on its own
steps.stepSummary: רבי ישמעאל uses 'או' to separate the cases, so one is חייב even for offering up just one of them.
steps.simpleTranslation: To separate them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that for רבי ישמעאל, the word 'or' teaches that each kind of קרבן counts separately.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without 'או,' someone might think he is חייב only if he offers up both an עולה and a זבח. The word 'or' shows that offering up either one alone makes him חייב.

keyTerms.meaning: To separate. Each item makes one חייב by itself.

steps.whatToRemember: For רבי ישמעאל, 'או זבח' teaches that each act counts on its own. Sprinkling, for him, comes from 'דם יחשב.'

phrases.english: To separate them.
phrases.notes: He means that offering up only an עולה, or only a זבח, is already enough to be חייב.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question from step 10.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'או' teaches that each case counts separately.

steps.title: Where does רבי עקיבא learn to count each case separately?
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא used 'או זבח' for sprinkling blood. So the גמרא asks where he learns that each act makes one חייב on its own.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי עקיבא, where does he learn that the cases are counted separately?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to רבי עקיבא. It asks where he gets the rule of 'dividing' the cases, since he already used the word 'או' for something else.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 11, רבי ישמעאל learned from 'או' that offering up even one item makes a person חייב. רבי עקיבא used 'או זבח' to teach the law of sprinkling blood (Step 9). So he needs a different source for the dividing rule.

keyTerms.meaning: To divide: each case counts on its own, so one is חייב even for just one of them
From where does he learn it?

phrases.english: And Rabbi Akiva,
from where does he learn to divide the cases?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the question from Step 10 around: now the גמרא asks about רבי עקיבא's source for the rule רבי ישמעאל learned from 'או'.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The verse רבי עקיבא uses for the rule that each case counts separately.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא learns it from 'he will not bring it'
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא learns the dividing rule from the singular word 'יביאנו' ('bring it').
steps.simpleTranslation: He learns it from 'לא יביאנו', 'he will not bring it'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי עקיבא learns the dividing rule from the words 'לא יביאנו' in the next פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'It' is singular. That shows a person is חייב even if he brings up just one item. So רבי עקיבא gets the same rule as רבי ישמעאל, only from a different word.

keyTerms.meaning: He learns it from
'He will not bring it' (ויקרא 17:9)
The ending meaning 'it', in the singular

phrases.english: He learns it from 'he will not bring it.'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 17:9. The point is the singular 'it': even one item is enough to make him חייב.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 12.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי עקיבא learns from the singular 'יביאנו' that each item counts on its own.

steps.title: רבי ישמעאל needs 'it' to teach that only a complete offering counts
steps.stepSummary: רבי ישמעאל does not use 'לא יביאנו' for the dividing rule. He needs it to teach that one is חייב only for a complete offering, not an incomplete one.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי ישמעאל needs that word to teach: one is חייב for a complete offering, but not for an incomplete one.
steps.whatsHappening: Behind this line is an unspoken question: why doesn't רבי ישמעאל learn the dividing rule from 'לא יביאנו'? The גמרא answers that he needs that word for a different law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי ישמעאל, 'it' means the whole thing. So a person is חייב only if he offers up a complete item outside. This new rule now has to be accounted for in רבי עקיבא's view too.

keyTerms.meaning: He needs it (for a different teaching)
Complete, whole
Incomplete, missing a part

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yishmael:
phrases.notes: The question 'why doesn't he use לא יביאנו?' is left unsaid. The גמרא jumps straight to the answer.

phrases.english: he needs that word for something else:
for a complete offering he is liable,
but he is not liable for an incomplete one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why רבי ישמעאל does not use רבי עקיבא's source from Step 13.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי ישמעאל uses 'יביאנו' to teach that one is חייב only for a complete offering.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא learns the 'complete offering' rule from 'to sacrifice it'
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא learns the complete-offering rule from the second 'it' in the פסוק, 'לעשות אתו'.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי עקיבא learns that rule from 'לעשות אותו', 'to sacrifice it'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that רבי עקיבא also has a source for the complete-offering rule. He uses the next words of the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says 'it' twice: 'יביאנו' and 'לעשות אתו'. רבי עקיבא uses the first for dividing and the second for the complete-offering rule. So he has used up both words.

keyTerms.meaning: 'To sacrifice it' (ויקרא 17:9), the second 'it' in the פסוק

phrases.english: And Rabbi Akiva:
he learns it from 'to sacrifice it.'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 17:9 again. This is a second 'it' in the same פסוק.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא – נָפְקָא לֵיהּ מִ״לַּעֲשׂוֹת אוֹתוֹ״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives רבי עקיבא's source for the rule רבי ישמעאל taught in Step 14.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי עקיבא learns the complete-offering rule from 'לעשות אתו'.

steps.title: רבי ישמעאל uses both words for two kinds of incomplete offerings
steps.stepSummary: רבי ישמעאל uses the two 'it' words to exempt two different cases. In one, offerings fit for burning inside became incomplete. In the other, offerings meant to be burned outside became incomplete. Both were offered up outside.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי ישמעאל: one word teaches about parts meant to be burned inside that became incomplete and were offered up outside. The other teaches about parts meant to be burned outside that became incomplete and were offered up outside.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains what רבי ישמעאל does with the second 'it' ('לעשות אתו'). He uses each 'it' for a different case where one is פטור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'מוקטרי פנים' are parts fit to be burned on the inner מזבח. 'מוקטרי חוץ' are unfit parts, such as from an animal slaughtered outside. רבי ישמעאל holds that if either kind became incomplete and was offered outside, there is no חיוב.

keyTerms.meaning: Parts fit to be burned inside, on the מזבח in the עזרה
Parts that will be burned outside because they are unfit, like from an animal slaughtered outside
He offered them up
Outside the עזרה

steps.confusionAlert: 'Burned inside' and 'burned outside' describe what kind of offering it is: fit for the מזבח or not. In both cases, the act being discussed is offering it up OUTSIDE.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yishmael:
phrases.notes: The unspoken question: what does he do with 'לעשות אתו'?

phrases.english: one is for parts meant to be burned inside that became incomplete
and he offered them up outside,
and one is for parts meant to be burned outside that became incomplete
and he offered them up outside.
phrases.notes: Some versions say 'והעלו' (round brackets). The corrected wording is 'והעלן', 'he offered them up' (square brackets).

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל – חַד לְמוּקְטְרֵי פְּנִים שֶׁחָסְרוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows that רבי ישמעאל also has a use for 'לעשות אתו', just as רבי עקיבא does.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Each 'it' exempts a different kind of incomplete offering that was offered up outside.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports רבי ישמעאל
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes רבי ישמעאל using 'לעשות אתו' to exempt parts fit for burning inside that became incomplete and were offered up outside.
steps.simpleTranslation: And so a ברייתא teaches: רבי ישמעאל says, you might think that if parts meant to be burned inside became incomplete and were offered up outside, he is חייב. The פסוק says 'לעשות אתו': he is חייב for a complete one, not for an incomplete one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to back up what it just said about רבי ישמעאל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא shows that רבי ישמעאל himself used 'לעשות אתו' for incomplete parts meant for burning inside. This confirms the reading in Step 16.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have thought
Therefore the פסוק says

phrases.english: And so it is taught in a baraita:
Rabbi Yishmael says:
One might think that parts meant to be burned inside that became incomplete
and he offered them up outside, he is liable?
The verse states: 'to sacrifice it':
for a complete one he is liable,
but he is not liable for an incomplete one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports Step 16 with a ברייתא in רבי ישמעאל's name.
steps.raayaObject: רבי ישמעאל's use of 'לעשות אתו' to exempt incomplete parts meant for burning inside.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא holds one is liable for incomplete parts fit for burning inside
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא has no extra word left to exempt this case. So he holds one is חייב for parts fit for burning inside that became incomplete and were offered up outside.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי עקיבא holds: parts meant to be burned inside that became incomplete and were offered up outside, he is חייב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא states the result of the whole discussion: in this case רבי עקיבא disagrees with רבי ישמעאל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא used both 'it' words: one for dividing, one for the complete-offering rule. So no word is left to exempt incomplete parts that were fit for burning inside, and he holds one is חייב for them.

keyTerms.meaning: Liable to punishment (here, כרת)
That became incomplete

steps.whatToRemember: Both תנאים read 'לא יביאנו' and 'לעשות אתו' differently. רבי ישמעאל: 'או' divides the cases, and both 'it' words exempt incomplete offerings. רבי עקיבא: 'יביאנו' divides the cases and 'אתו' teaches the complete-offering rule. So he holds one is חייב for incomplete parts that were fit for burning inside.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Akiva:
parts meant to be burned inside that became incomplete
and he offered them up outside, he is liable.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sets רבי עקיבא's ruling against רבי ישמעאל's view, which the ברייתא in Step 17 supported.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי עקיבא holds one is חייב for incomplete parts fit for burning inside that were offered up outside. רבי ישמעאל holds he is פטור.

steps.title: What does רבי עקיבא do with 'blood shall be imputed'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how רבי עקיבא uses the words 'דם יחשב', since רבי ישמעאל used them for sprinkling blood outside.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי עקיבא, what does he learn from the words 'דם יחשב'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to רבי עקיבא and asks what he does with the words 'דם יחשב'. This sets up the next step, where the answer comes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, רבי ישמעאל used 'דם יחשב' to make someone חייב for sprinkling blood outside. רבי עקיבא learns that law another way. So the גמרא asks what these words teach him, since no word in the תורה is extra.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Blood shall be imputed', words from the פסוק about slaughtering outside (ויקרא 17:4)
What does he do with it? (What does he learn from it?)

phrases.english: And Rabbi Akiva,
this 'blood shall be imputed', what does he do with it?
phrases.notes: ויקרא 17:4. רבי ישמעאל used these words for sprinkling blood outside, so what does רבי עקיבא learn from them?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא, הַאי ״דָּם יֵחָשֵׁב״ מַאי עָבֵיד לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After settling how each תנא uses 'אתו', the גמרא moves on to another phrase, 'דם יחשב'.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What רבי עקיבא learns from 'דם יחשב', since he does not use it for sprinkling.

steps.title: It includes slaughtering a bird outside
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא uses 'דם יחשב' to include slaughtering a bird offering outside.
steps.simpleTranslation: To include slaughtering a bird.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי עקיבא uses 'דם יחשב' to make someone חייב for slaughtering a bird offering outside.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Inside the מקדש a bird is not slaughtered. It is killed by מליקה (pinching the neck). So you might think slaughtering a bird outside is not a real 'offering' act. 'דם יחשב' teaches that one is still חייב.

keyTerms.meaning: To include (to add a case to the law)
Slaughtering a bird

phrases.english: To include the slaughter of a bird.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 19.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי עקיבא uses 'דם יחשב' to make one חייב for slaughtering a bird outside.

steps.title: רבי ישמעאל learns bird slaughter from 'or that slaughters'
steps.stepSummary: רבי ישמעאל, who used 'דם יחשב' for sprinkling, learns the bird slaughter law from 'או אשר ישחט'.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי ישמעאל learns it from 'או אשר ישחט'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains where רבי ישמעאל gets the law of slaughtering a bird outside, since he used 'דם יחשב' for something else.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both תנאים agree one is חייב for slaughtering a bird outside. They only argue about which words teach it. For רבי ישמעאל, the extra word 'או' ('or') adds the bird.

keyTerms.meaning: He learns it from
'Or that slaughters', words from ויקרא 17:3

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yishmael –
he derives it from 'or that slaughters.'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 17:3

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל נָפְקָא לֵיהּ מֵ״אוֹ אֲשֶׁר יִשְׁחָט״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the hidden question: if רבי ישמעאל uses 'דם יחשב' for sprinkling, where does he learn the bird slaughter law?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי ישמעאל learns slaughtering a bird outside from 'או אשר ישחט'.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא needs 'or that slaughters' to exclude pinching
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא does not learn bird slaughter from 'או אשר ישחט', because he needs it to teach that only slaughtering a bird outside makes one חייב, not pinching it.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי עקיבא would tell you: he needs that פסוק to teach that one is חייב for slaughtering, but not for pinching.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why רבי עקיבא does not use 'או אשר ישחט' the way רבי ישמעאל does. He needs it for another rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי עקיבא, the word 'ישחט' ('slaughters') teaches a limit: only slaughtering counts outside. So someone who does מליקה (pinches) a bird outside is פטור. That is why he needs a different source, 'דם יחשב', to include bird slaughter.

keyTerms.meaning: Would say to you (how he would answer)
He needs it (for something else)
One who pinches a bird's neck, the way a bird is offered inside

steps.confusionAlert: It sounds strange: inside the מקדש, pinching is the correct way to offer a bird. Yet doing it outside does not make one חייב here. Only slaughtering a bird outside does.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Akiva would say to you,
that one is needed by him:
phrases.notes: 'That one' means 'או אשר ישחט'.

phrases.english: for one who slaughters he is liable,
but not for one who pinches.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אָמַר לָךְ, הַהוּא מִיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why רבי עקיבא does not take רבי ישמעאל's source from step 21.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי עקיבא uses 'או אשר ישחט' to exempt pinching a bird outside.

steps.title: רבי ישמעאל learns the pinching exemption from 'this is the matter'
steps.stepSummary: רבי ישמעאל learns that pinching outside is פטור from the words 'זה הדבר'.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי ישמעאל learns it from 'זה הדבר'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells us where רבי ישמעאל learns that pinching a bird outside is פטור, since he used 'או אשר ישחט' for bird slaughter.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'זה' ('this') points to one specific act: slaughtering, and nothing else. So for רבי ישמעאל, 'זה הדבר' leaves out pinching. Both תנאים agree on the law. They only differ on the source.

keyTerms.meaning: 'This is the matter', words from ויקרא 17:2

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yishmael –
he derives it from 'this is the matter.'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 17:2. 'It' here is the rule that pinching outside is פטור.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל נָפְקָא לֵיהּ מִ״זֶּה הַדָּבָר״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the hidden question: where does רבי ישמעאל learn the pinching exemption?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי ישמעאל learns the pinching exemption from 'זה הדבר'.

steps.title: A ברייתא: 'or that slaughters' includes a bird
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא supports רבי ישמעאל. 'אשר ישחט' alone teaches an animal, and 'או אשר ישחט' adds a bird.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: 'That slaughters' teaches only one who slaughters an animal. How do we know one who slaughtered a bird? The פסוק says 'or that slaughters'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that learns the way רבי ישמעאל does. This first part shows bird slaughter learned from 'או אשר ישחט'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק talks about an ox, a lamb, or a goat, which are all animals. The added 'או' ('or') stretches the law to a bird too. This matches רבי ישמעאל's source from step 21.

keyTerms.meaning: I only know (this case so far)
From where do we know?
The פסוק says (to teach us)

phrases.english: As it is taught in a baraita:
'That slaughters' –
phrases.notes: ויקרא 17:3

phrases.english: I have only one who slaughters an animal;
if he slaughtered a bird, from where do we know?
The verse says: 'or that slaughters.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא that matches רבי ישמעאל's sources.
steps.raayaObject: רבי ישמעאל's source for bird slaughter outside: 'או אשר ישחט'.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא that uses 'או אשר ישחט' to include a bird.

steps.title: Logic suggests pinching outside should also make one liable
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא suggests a קל וחומר: if slaughtering a bird, which is not the way inside, makes one חייב, then pinching, which is the way inside, should surely make one חייב.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might think even one who pinches is חייב. And it makes sense: slaughter is not how a bird is made fit inside, yet one is חייב for it. Pinching is how a bird is made fit inside, so isn't it logical that one is חייב for it?
steps.whatsHappening: Inside the same ברייתא, a strong logical argument is raised that pinching outside should also make one חייב. This sets up the פסוק that will reject it in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a קל וחומר. Slaughtering a bird is the 'weaker' case, since it is not even the correct method inside, and yet one is חייב. Pinching is the 'stronger' case, since it is the real method inside, so logic says it should make one חייב even more.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have thought
And it is logical (a reasoned argument)
Its proper method of preparation
Inside (the עזרה of the מקדש)

phrases.english: One might think even one who pinches?
And it is logical:

phrases.aramaic: מָה שְׁחִיטָה דְּאֵין דֶּרֶךְ הֶכְשֵׁירָהּ בִּפְנִים, חַיָּיב,
phrases.english: if slaughter, which is not its method of preparation inside, he is liable,
pinching, which is its method of preparation inside,
is it not logical that he is liable?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After including bird slaughter, the ברייתא asks if pinching should be included too.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that only slaughtering a bird outside makes one חייב.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: קל וחומר: if the method that is not used inside makes one חייב, the method that is used inside should surely do so.

steps.title: 'This is the matter' excludes pinching
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא rejects the logical argument with 'זה הדבר': only slaughtering makes one חייב, not pinching.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says 'זה הדבר'.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא ends by quoting 'זה הדבר' to cancel the קל וחומר. Pinching a bird outside does not make one חייב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק's word 'זה' ('this') limits the law to slaughtering only. This shows the ברייתא learns the pinching exemption from 'זה הדבר', just as רבי ישמעאל does in step 23.

keyTerms.meaning: Pinching the back of a bird's neck, the way a bird is offered inside

steps.whatToRemember: Both תנאים agree: slaughtering a bird outside makes one חייב, and pinching it outside does not. רבי עקיבא learns these from 'דם יחשב' and 'או אשר ישחט'. רבי ישמעאל learns them from 'או אשר ישחט' and 'זה הדבר', like the ברייתא.

phrases.english: The verse says: 'this is the matter.'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 17:2. 'This' means only slaughtering, so pinching is left out.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the קל וחומר of step 25 using a פסוק.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Pinching a bird outside is פטור, learned from 'זה הדבר'. This supports רבי ישמעאל's source.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא needs 'this is the matter' for a different teaching
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא does not learn the פטור for pinching from 'זה הדבר', because he uses those words for a גזירה שוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי עקיבא would tell you: he needs that verse for a גזירה שוה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why רבי עקיבא does not use the words 'זה הדבר' the way רבי ישמעאל and the ברייתא did. He uses those words for something else.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי ישמעאל and the ברייתא learned from 'זה הדבר' that pinching outside is פטור. רבי עקיבא answers that 'זה הדבר' is needed for a גזירה שוה, so it cannot teach the pinching rule. That is why he learns the pinching exemption from 'או אשר ישחט' instead (Step 22).

keyTerms.meaning: A teaching learned by comparing two places in the תורה that use the same word or phrase
He needs it (for another teaching)
He would say to you

steps.whatToRemember: Both sides agree that pinching outside is פטור. רבי ישמעאל learns it from 'זה הדבר'. רבי עקיבא learns it from 'או אשר ישחט' and uses 'זה הדבר' for a גזירה שוה.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Akiva would say to you:
That verse is needed by him for a verbal analogy.
phrases.notes: 'That' means the words 'זה הדבר'. The same words also appear in the section about vows (במדבר 30:2).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why רבי עקיבא does not use the 'זה הדבר' derivation from the ברייתא in Steps 23-26.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי עקיבא uses 'זה הדבר' for a גזירה שוה, so it is not available to teach that pinching is פטור.

steps.title: Source for exemption when taking a handful or collecting blood outside
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source of the משנה's rule that one who takes a handful from a מנחה or collects blood outside is פטור.
steps.simpleTranslation: And about what we learned in the משנה, that one who takes a handful or collects blood outside is פטור: where do we learn this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic. It quotes a משנה and asks for the source of its rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: קמיצה (taking a handful) and קבלה (collecting the blood) are real steps of the עבודה. The משנה says doing them outside, without finishing the עבודה, is פטור. The גמרא wants to know how we know that.

keyTerms.meaning: One who takes a handful from a מנחה offering
One who collects the blood of a קרבן in a vessel

phrases.english: And that which we learned in a mishna:
One who takes a handful or collects blood outside is exempt –
From where do we derive this?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the topic of birds to a new question about other עבודות done outside.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source showing that one who takes a handful or collects blood outside is פטור.

steps.title: Why would we ever think he is liable?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא is surprised by the question: there was never a reason to think he is חייב, so why look for a source that he is פטור?
steps.simpleTranslation: But from where would you learn that he is חייב?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges its own question. Normally you are פטור unless a source makes you חייב, so the question seems unnecessary.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The burden of proof is on the side that says חייב. If no source makes him חייב, he is automatically פטור. This line sets up the next two steps, which test whether a source for חייב could exist.

keyTerms.meaning: And from where would it come?
Liable (to punishment)

phrases.english: But from where would it be derived that he is liable?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Pushes back on the question in Step 28.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Being פטור needs no source. Only being חייב needs one, so asking for the source of the פטור seems unnecessary.

steps.title: Cannot learn liability from slaughtering
steps.stepSummary: Someone might try to learn חיוב from שחיטה outside. But שחיטה is stricter, because a פסח becomes פסול through שחיטה for people who cannot eat it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Should we learn it from שחיטה? What about שחיטה: it is special, because a פסח becomes פסול when slaughtered for people who cannot eat it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests one possible way to make קמיצה and קבלה חייב: compare them to שחיטה outside. It knocks that comparison down.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Slaughtering outside is חייב even without finishing the עבודה, so it looks like a good model. But שחיטה has a strictness that קמיצה and קבלה do not have: intending the פסח for non-eaters makes it פסול at the שחיטה. Since שחיטה is stricter, we cannot copy its חיוב onto the weaker steps.

keyTerms.meaning: What about X? It is special because... (a formula used to refute a comparison)
For people who cannot eat the קרבן
The קרבן פסח (Passover offering)
Becomes disqualified

phrases.english: Let it be derived from slaughtering –
What is special about slaughtering?
That a Paschal offering is disqualified through it when done for those who cannot eat it!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Backs up Step 29 by showing that שחיטה cannot be a source for חיוב.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects learning חיוב for קמיצה and קבלה from שחיטה.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: שחיטה has an extra strictness in פסח (it is ruined by intent for non-eaters) that קמיצה and קבלה lack.

steps.title: Cannot learn liability from sprinkling
steps.stepSummary: Someone might try to learn חיוב from זריקה outside. But זריקה is stricter, because a זר who does it in the מקדש gets מיתה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Should we learn it from זריקה? What about זריקה: it is special, because a זר is חייב מיתה for it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests the second possible model, זריקה (sprinkling blood), and rejects it too. That finishes its point: there was never a source to make him חייב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Sprinkling is only one step of the עבודה, yet doing it outside is חייב, so it looks like a good model. But a זר who does זריקה is חייב מיתה בידי שמים, which is a strictness קמיצה and קבלה do not have. With both models rejected, there is no reason to think he is חייב, so his פטור needs no source.

keyTerms.meaning: Sprinkling the blood on the מזבח
A non-כהן
Death (here, death by the hand of Heaven)

steps.whatToRemember: No source makes קמיצה or קבלה outside חייב. שחיטה is stricter because of פסח, and זריקה is stricter because a זר gets מיתה. So the משנה's פטור needs no special source.

phrases.english: Let it be derived from sprinkling –
What is special about sprinkling?
That a non-priest is liable to death for it!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the argument of Step 30 by rejecting the second possible model.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects learning חיוב for קמיצה and קבלה from זריקה.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: זריקה carries מיתה for a זר, a strictness that קמיצה and קבלה lack.
